name: Lizard

modes.label: Sandbox (4 vCPU / 4 GiB, flat per second while it runs)
modes.note: Pricing page FAQ (checked 2026-10-01): "Small (2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM) at $0.009/hour, Medium (4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM) at $0.018/hour, and Large (8 vCPU, 16 GB RAM) at $0.036/hour. Medium is the default. CPU and memory are included, and so is sandbox egress up to 2 TB per account over a rolling 30 days; Persistent Volumes cost extra." Billed by the second including idle time. These flat rates are about a tenth of Lizard's own published per-resource rates ($0.000006948 per vCPU-s = $0.025/vCPU-h, $0.000003474 per GB-s = $0.0125/GB-h, i.e. ~$0.10/h for 2 vCPU / 4 GB). The sandbox docs say current sandboxes have fixed limits of 4 vCPU / 4096 MiB that create options don't change; the sizes are priced as published. Modelled as the only size the docs confirm: Medium (the default) at $0.018/h, delivering the documented fixed 4 vCPU / 4 GiB. Small (2 vCPU / 4 GB, $0.009/h) and Large (8 vCPU / 16 GB, $0.036/h) are left out until the runtime honours sizes.

plans.name: Free trial
plans.note: $10 in free credits, valid for 7 days. "During the free trial you can run 5 sandboxes at once and start 6 per minute, 30 per hour and 100 per day."

plans.name: After a first top-up
plans.note: Pay as you go, no subscription: "Your first top-up of any amount raises that to 20 at once and doubles the start rates."

plans.name: After $20 paid in total
plans.note: "Once you have paid $20 in total, it becomes 100 at once and the start rates double again. Limits count across all your workspaces, and paused sandboxes do not count as running. For more, contact us about Enterprise." The highest self-serve limit is 100 at once.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Billing terms agreed in a contract; custom limits, SOC 2 & HIPAA, SSO/SAML, RBAC & audit log, dedicated nodes.

extras.price: $0.000000054 per GB-s (~$0.14/GB-month), billed on used space while you keep the data; 1-50 GB, node-local storage

isolation.quote: Sandboxes run short-lived commands and agent tasks in Kubernetes pods with the runc runtime. They share the host kernel; they are not Firecracker virtual machines.

ssh.quote: SSH access is not available for the current runtime.
ssh.note: The sandboxes landing page advertises `lizard sandbox ssh`.

pause_resume.quote: Pause, resume, fork, snapshot, restore, and file watching currently return HTTP 501.
pause_resume.note: The landing page advertises pause/resume and snapshot/restore.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Pause, resume, fork, snapshot, restore, and file watching currently return HTTP 501.

fork.quote: Pause, resume, fork, snapshot, restore, and file watching currently return HTTP 501.

custom_image.quote: The public CLI does not provide a custom-template upload flow.

persistent_disk.quote: A volume in Lizard (lizard.build) keeps data after a sandbox stops. It mounts at /workspace and attaches to one sandbox at a time.
persistent_disk.note: Volumes use node-local storage; Lizard says to export data you need after a node failure.

desktop.note: The landing page advertises `lizard sandbox desktop` ("Full desktop in your browser"); the docs list no desktop template.

harness_api.quote: sandbox.process.exec(cmd) | Run a shell command; return stdout, stderr, and exitCode.
harness_api.note: The landing page advertises `lizard sandbox prompt` (Run Claude Code or Codex); the SDK reference has no such method.

inbound_https.quote: sandbox.getHost(port) | Register a public HTTPS hostname for a port.

eu_data_residency.quote: Regional deployment Launch in US East or EU West. Choose where your agent runs.

caveats: Container isolation: sandboxes are Kubernetes pods on runc sharing the host kernel, not VMs.

The landing page advertises SSH, pause/resume, snapshot/restore, a desktop and a Claude Code / Codex prompt command; the SDK reference says SSH is not available, that pause, resume, fork, snapshot and restore return HTTP 501, and lists no desktop template or prompt method.

Sizes: the pricing page sells Small 2 vCPU / 4 GB ($0.009/h), Medium 4 / 8 ($0.018/h) and Large 8 / 16 ($0.036/h), but the SDK reference says current sandboxes have fixed limits of 4 vCPU and 4096 MiB that create options don't change. Priced here as Medium at what the docs say you get: 4 vCPU / 4 GiB.
The flat sandbox rates are about a tenth of Lizard's own per-resource rates (CPU $0.025/vCPU-h, memory $0.0125/GB-h).
Self-serve limit is 100 sandboxes at once (after $20 paid in total); more needs Enterprise. The landing calculator goes up to 2,000 at once.
Persistent Volumes are node-local and attach to one sandbox at a time.
Public usage counter (lizard.build/api/public/stats, 2026-10-01): 436 workspaces, 8,870 sandbox starts in total.

fleet.notes: Start caps: trial 6/min, 30/hour, 100/day; doubled after the first top-up; doubled again after $20 paid. Limits count across all workspaces.
